seoTitle: How to Export Your Google Workspace Data and Back It Up
metaDescription: Back up or export Google Workspace data using Google Takeout or the Admin Console, covering Gmail, Drive, Calendar, and shared drive files for every user.
intro: Whether you're switching accounts, backing up company data, or preparing to offboard a user, exporting Google Workspace data is something every admin eventually needs to do. This guide covers the two very different paths available: an individual exporting their own Gmail, Drive, and Calendar data through Google Takeout, and an admin pulling data across the whole organization for backup or compliance purposes. It closes with the practical choices around export format, destination, and what to check before you delete anyone's account.

steps.heading: Export your own data with Google Takeout
steps.body: Any user can go to Google Takeout and select exactly which services to include — Gmail, Drive, Calendar, Photos, and dozens of others are each listed individually with a checkbox, so you're not forced to download everything if you only need one or two services. Takeout packages the result into downloadable archive files, typically zip, and can deliver them straight to a linked cloud storage account instead of your local device if the file size is large.

steps.heading: Check that Google Vault is enabled for org-wide retention
steps.body: For anything beyond a single user's self-service export, the tool that matters is Google Vault, one of the core services listed and toggled from the Admin Console's app service status screen alongside Meet, Groups, Keep, and Sites. Vault is what gives admins retention and export capability over mail, Drive files, and chat messages across the whole organization, rather than relying on each employee to run their own Takeout. If Vault shows as off for any organizational unit here, admin-level exports for those users won't be available until it's turned on.

image.caption: The Admin Console's service status list, with Google Vault switched on alongside Meet, Groups, Keep, and Sites — Vault is the service admin-level exports depend on.

steps.heading: Run an admin-level export across your users
steps.body: With Vault enabled, an admin can pull data for specific users or the entire organization rather than exporting one account at a time. This is the path to take for a genuine backup or a legal hold, since it captures data even from accounts a user might not think to export themselves, and it doesn't require cooperation from each individual employee.

steps.heading: Remember what Takeout actually bundles together
steps.body: The services you can pull into a single Takeout or admin export map directly to the core Workspace apps — Drive, Gmail, and Calendar chief among them, plus whatever else is active on the account. Knowing this list up front helps you scope the export correctly instead of guessing: if all you need is someone's calendar history, there's no reason to also pull years of Drive files into the same archive.

image.caption: The Google apps switcher, listing Drive, Gmail, Calendar, Docs, Sheets, and Slides — the same core services a Takeout or admin export can include.

steps.heading: Handle shared drive files separately
steps.body: Shared drive content behaves differently from a personal My Drive, since ownership belongs to the shared drive itself rather than any one user. Before offboarding someone who manages or heavily uses a shared drive, confirm their files there are captured by the admin export and that drive membership is reassigned so the shared drive doesn't lose its last manager when the account is deleted.

steps.heading: Choose a destination and format, then verify before deleting anyone
steps.body: Both Takeout and admin exports let you choose where the archive lands — local download, or delivery to a linked Drive or another connected cloud storage account — and which file format works best for how you'll actually use the data later. The one non-negotiable step: open and spot-check the completed export before deleting or offboarding the account it came from. An export that silently failed or missed a service is much easier to fix while the original account still exists than after.

faq.question: Can I export just one user's Gmail and Drive data?
faq.answer: Yes, Google Takeout lets an individual user select and export their own Gmail, Drive, Calendar, and other Workspace data without any admin involvement.

faq.question: How do I back up data for every user in my organization?
faq.answer: Admin-level exports require Google Vault to be enabled, which is toggled from the Admin Console's service status screen alongside other core apps like Meet and Sites.

faq.question: Should I export a user's data before offboarding them?
faq.answer: Yes, and just as important, verify the export actually completed and includes everything expected before you delete the account — fixing a missed export is far harder afterward.

faq.question: Can I export shared drive files as well as personal ones?
faq.answer: Yes, but shared drive content is owned by the shared drive rather than any individual, so confirm it's captured separately and that drive membership is reassigned before offboarding a manager.
